source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 10 mathematics textbooks (general stream)

stages.headline: Infinite non-periodic decimals are irrational numbers, e.g. √2 = 1.4142..., π = 3.1415...; rationals and irrationals together form the real numbers ℝ.
stages.headlineEnglish: Infinite non-periodic decimals are irrational numbers, e.g. √2 = 1.4142..., π = 3.1415...; rationals and irrationals together form the real numbers ℝ.

stages.headline: Each point of the number line corresponds to exactly one real number and vice versa; the point √2 is found with the diagonal of a unit square.
stages.headlineEnglish: Each point of the number line corresponds to exactly one real number and vice versa; the point √2 is found with the diagonal of a unit square.

stages.headline: Reals are compared through their decimals: √5 = 2.236... > 2.2; a rational plus an irrational is irrational.
stages.headlineEnglish: Reals are compared through their decimals: √5 = 2.236... > 2.2; a rational plus an irrational is irrational.
